In a recent development, but, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage. Instead the public prosecutor's office appeared to be more interested in the activities of her German employer, the Heinrich Böll Foundation.

For 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator. In her role, she organizes projects that focus on democracy and the rights of women, minorities and LGBTQ+ people.

It has been revealed that during the interrogation, transfers of money from the foundation into her bank account were discussed. Verdioglu Sik found out that she was now also subject to a travel ban.

Recent findings suggest that verdioglu Sik was eventually released, but her arrest caused outrage among critics of the Turkish government. She is married to investigative journalist and member of parliament, Ahmet Sik. He belongs to the left-wing Workers' Party of Turkey, or TIP, and is known as one of the harshest critics of the current government.

Sik has recently been looking into a stock market scandal, which allegedly benefited members of the ruling Justice and Development Party, or AKP, headed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and associates.

According to recent reports, opposition critics drew a clear conclusion: As a member of parliament, Sik has parliamentary immunity. So instead, the justice system is putting pressure on him through his wife.

"If you take away a state's law, what is left is no longer called a state, but a gang," Sik responded to the arrest in writing.

Sources indicate that verdioglu Sik's arrest is not the first such case in Turkey. Ever since the attempted coup against the Erdogan government in 2016, accusations of espionage have been leveled at a wide variety of groups in Turkey: journalists, opposition figures and human rights activists as well as employees of foreign embassies and staff of foreign institutions like nongovernmental organizations and foundations.

Such accusations have often been followed by acquittals or convictions for other offenses, albeit sometimes years later. But what the many instances have in common is what's known as a "chilling effect." Any investigation can mean lengthy pre-trial detention, reputational and professional damage and even social isolation.

In the past, such cases have even triggered diplomatic spats.

It has been revealed that in 2015, for example, Can Dundar and Erdem Gul, both senior journalists at the opposition daily Cumhuriyet, were accused of espionage after reporting that Turkey had tried to ship arms to rebels fighting the Syrian government. Dundar now lives in exile in Berlin.

In 2017, Erdogan said that reporter Deniz Yücel, then working for German newspaper Die Welt, was a "German agent." That led to a serious diplomatic crisis between Berlin and Ankara.

Espionage charges have also been laid against local employees of the US diplomatic corps and against a lawyer working for the German embassy. US pastor Andrew Brunson and his wife were also arrested because of alleged links to Kurdish anti-government groups. Turkish philanthropist and human rights activist Osman Kavala, who was charged with espionage and attempting to overthrow the constitutional order, remains in prison.

Most recently, espionage charges have been brought against the former Istanbul mayor and Erdogan's political competitor, Ekrem Imamoglu, and a number of journalists.

Hakki Tas, a research fellow and expert on Turkey at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies, said the number of such cases have been increasing over the past few years.

It has been revealed that on the one hand, Turkey has the right to protect itself from foreign intelligence services — especially given geopolitical competition and conflict in the region, he argued. On the other hand, there's a long tradition of bringing the Turkish opposition to court to face security charges.

"What foreigners or employees of foreign institutions have experienced in recent years is a continuation of this pattern," Tas told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that media outlets and NGOs critical of the government have faced investigations, trials and other sorts of state sanctions for years. The ruling AKP party has also brought in its own version of a so-called "foreign agent law.".

These sorts of espionage cases serve both a domestic and foreign policy function, Tas mentioned.

For locals, "contact with a foreign institution, foreign funding or even a perfectly normal salary could become part of an investigation someday," he explained. "For opposition figures and civil society organizations, in particular, this can become a security issue.".

It has been revealed that in terms of foreign policy, the cases also show other countries that there are limits to their activities inside Turkey. These kinds of accusations seem to become more frequent when there's some sort of foreign policy tension — for example, after Western criticism of how opposition groups were dealt with after the alleged coup in 2016, the aforementioned disputes about arms deliveries in connection with Syria, or criticism from abroad about the removal of elected mayors in Turkey.

It can also serve as a kind of "hostage diplomacy," Tas stated.

The case of US pastor Brunson is a good example. After his arrest, the Turkish government proposed a trade with the Americans. They wanted to exchange Turkish preacher Fethullah Gulen, who lived in the US and who the Turkish government blamed for the 2016 coup attempt.

This suspicion of foreign institutions isn't something that the Erdogan government invented, Tas points out. In the early 2000s, several representatives of German organizations were already made to stand trial in Turkey. At the time, it was alleged that, among other things, the German spy service was using German foundations as a front for conspiracy.

According to recent reports, in some of the best-known cases, defendants often don't end up convicted of espionage. In the case of activist Osman Kavala, he was initially acquitted of espionage several times and spent two years in prison, just because of those charges.

But Tas said that's no surprise, referring to a 1979 work about the sociology of law written by US law professor Malcolm Feeley. It's title: "The Process Is the Punishment.".

This article was originally written in German.

In a recent development, video Assistant Referee (VAR) has its fair share of critics. Introduced to the Premier League at the start of the 2019/20 season, the technology was designed to help the on-pitch officials and ensure matches were officiated seamlessly and without controversy.

Sources indicate that however, it has not had the impact that it was intended to have. If anything, the number of refereeing controversies has gone up, and many high-profile names, including Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney, have lost patience and want to see VAR scrapped.

But what would the 2026/27 Premier League table look like if every refereeing decision was correct? After every matchday in England's top tier, Squawka asks their followers to vote on controversial VAR decisions and whether the right decision was made or not.

Using that data, they have created a Premier League table without VAR errors following matchday 11, and it makes for interesting reading.

The table has been compiled on the basis that penalties, should they have been awarded, would have been converted.

According to recent reports, sunderland have had a dismal start to the campaign. The Black Cats, who are competing in the Conference League after finishing seventh in 2025/26, are currently 18th in the Premier League, having picked up nine points from their opening 11 games. They can be grateful for VAR that their troubles aren't any worse, though, as they would be rock bottom without its errors.

Sources indicate that crystal Palace would be second bottom, with Manchester United rounding out the relegation places, even after Leny Yoro had his red card overturned after he was wrongly sent off in a 4-0 defeat at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino's first game. Nottingham Forest, who are currently 17th in the Premier League, would be two points better off, though that wouldn't change their position.

The Premier League released a statement explaining the goal had been ruled out for handball, but many felt the footage was inconclusive and not clear and obvious. Had VAR made the right decision, Forest would have won 1-0.

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

Sources indicate that A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta noted, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

“There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

The result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

The Luis Milla curler into the far top corner proved enough for Como to see off AEK Athens and surge towards the Champions League Round of 16, despite Lucas Da Cunha’s missed penalty.

The Lariani had won three of their first four Champions League games, despite missing Moise Kean and Assane Diao, with Maxence Caqueret not at 100 per cent either, but Trevoh Chalobah returned five weeks after his muscular injury.

Industry observers note that AEK Athens lost their last three in Europe, but were leading Real Madrid twice until capitulating 3-2 in stoppages. Aboubakary Koita was sent off for dissent and therefore suspended, with midfielder Kervin Arriaga injured, but ex-Lazio goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha made his Champions League debut for this season after a wrist sprain.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Lazaros Rota made a decisive defensive block to stop Tasos Douvikas meeting the Nico Paz through ball at full stretch, then Stavros Pilios got back to block Nico Paz on the counter, but the Argentine was booked for flailing an elbow into the defender’s face.

There were a few technical problems with the referee’s communication system, both before kick-off and during the first half, but he didn’t need help from VAR when Lovro Majer was very late to trip Alex Valle in the box.

It has been revealed that however, Lucas Da Cunha slipped a little in the run-up and fired the penalty off target for Como. It was the first time in his career that the France international had failed to convert from the spot.

Jacobo Ramon couldn’t keep his header down from eight yards, and Alex Valle wasted a promising move with his scuffed finish past the near post.

Robert Sanchez needed a huge double save on the stroke of half-time, first on the Mijat Gacinovic deflected effort, then the Rota rebound too.

AEK had a huge chance after the restart, but Milan Vitalis couldn’t keep the finish down under pressure from a promising position after doing such good work to get into that situation.

Luis Milla with an unbelievable strike to give Como the lead 🥵.

Como survived the scares and took the lead when Luis Milla bent a right-foot curler into the far top corner from outside the area, on the Martin Baturina lay-off.

Nico Paz so nearly made it 2-0 when AEK gave it away playing out from the back, so Valle sent the Argentine through to clip the base of the near post.

Jacobo Ramon’s header was just wide on a free kick, with the same for the Moukoudi attempt on a free kick from ex-Cagliari midfielder Razvan Marin.

Maxi Perrone had a great chance to add another in the final minute, but was denied by a desperate one-handed Strakosha save.

Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.
  • Industry observers note that these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

Industry observers note that these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

In a recent development, biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he highlights little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the issues shaping the world today.

In his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

This outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish.

In a recent development, wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly noted in interviews. When the sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

Yet Biermann has noted his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. [...] Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama.".

Sources indicate that biermann's mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann once recalled. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism.".

According to recent reports, in 1953, while countless people were fleeing East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble, and also began writing and performing his political songs.

Industry observers note that biermann soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann said. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer.".

In 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Sources indicate that yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

On November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. ".

Sources indicate that I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

In a petition, leading East German intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

It has been revealed that "The SED leadership expected an angry media response from the West. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann wrote.

Afterward, Biermann sank into a deep depression. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he stated.

He became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he said. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom.".

The singer-songwriter plans to spend his 90th birthday at home in Hamburg with his wife and manager, Pamela. For the first time in his life, he noted, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children.

"I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency.

And should he ever die, he said, he wants to be buried at Berlin's cemetery where some renowned German writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them Bertolt Brecht, Anna Seghers and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, george Whitesides, a towering figure in chemistry who pushed chemists to cross boundaries to solve global problems, died on 19 November.
  • His son George, a US congressman representing California, confirmed Whitesides’s passing on the social media platform X, saying that the chemist died at home surrounded by family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

George Whitesides at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where he spent most of his academic career.Credit: Rick Friedman/Corbis via Getty.

According to recent reports, george Whitesides, a towering figure in chemistry who pushed chemists to cross boundaries to solve global problems, died on 19 November. He was 87.

His son George, a US congressman representing California, confirmed Whitesides’s passing on the social media platform X, saying that the chemist died at home surrounded by family.

Meet the soft, cuddly robots of the future.

Meet the soft, cuddly robots of the future.

Sources indicate that whitesides made landmark contributions to many fields: he was a pioneer in patterning surfaces with molecules, a technique that enabled ‘lab on a chip’ diagnostic devices, advances in nanotechnology and more. He prided himself on switching research interests often, telling students, “If somebody else is working on something, don’t work on it.”.

In a recent development, following the news of the chemist’s passing, messages celebrating his impact flooded online platforms. “I am so saddened to hear of his passing,” Zhenan Bao, a chemical engineer at Stanford University in California, wrote on LinkedIn. “George showed us that the most key problems don’t respect the lines between disciplines. He moved freely across chemistry, materials, biology, and engineering.”.

It has been revealed that whitesides trained hundreds of scientists who came through his laboratory, first at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and then at Harvard University, both in Cambridge. But he also inspired many others, says Joseph DeSimone, a polymer scientist at Stanford. In traditional chemistry departments, “there’s often a lot of pressure to stay in your lane, and he made it okay not to. In fact, he made it exciting not to”, DeSimone says.

Whitesides was born in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1939. One of his first experiences with chemistry was as a teenager, cleaning glassware at his father’s chemical engineering firm in his hometown.

After a bachelor’s degree in chemistry at Harvard, he enroled for a PhD at California Institute of Technology in Pasadena, studying how the workhorse chemicals known as Grignard reagents form and behave.

In a recent development, by 1963, Whitesides became a faculty member at MIT, where he would switch to studying the fundamentals of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs)1. These are tightly packed coatings of organic compounds that are a single-molecule thick, formed spontaneously because of forces drawing the molecules to a surface and to one another.

In a recent development, george Whitesides and his research group pioneered low-cost, paper-based microfluidic 'lab-on-a-chip' devices. Credit: Volker Steger/Science Photo Library.

From there, Whitesides saw ways of using SAMs to easily and cheaply create patterned surfaces — which at the time were often made with complicated lithography techniques involving light and ‘stencils’. He would go on to invent soft lithography2, which instead uses polymer stamps to transfer micro- and nanoscopic patterns of molecules to surfaces.

Industry observers note that this became an “enabling” research tool, claims John Rogers, a materials scientist at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, who was a postdoc with Whitesides at Harvard. The ability to easily pattern surfaces opened the door to creating 3D nanostructures, microfluidics and much more. It also “democratized” the ability to do this type of research, Rogers adds, because you no longer needed sophisticated cleanroom facilities and etching techniques to create such materials.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Allegri admits Napoli did something ‘really well for the first time’ in the 2-2 draw with Manchester City to keep Champions League ambition alive, and assures Kevin De Bruyne ‘will remain until June.’.

The Partenopei came to the Etihad fearing the worst amid an injury crisis that left them without 11 players between fitness, suspension and the Champions League list.

Instead, they leave here with regrets after twice taking the lead through Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, only to be clawed back by Ayyoub Bouaddi and the Rayan Cherki angled drive.

A 2-2 draw is still a positive result, especially away to Enzo Maresca’s side, and keeps them in the hunt for a play-off spot.

“This match was notable, because if we win at least one of the last three, we should be in a good position for qualification,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a very difficult game, the lads did well, and obviously there were moments when we had to suffer under pressure, but for the first time we really did well out of possession to slow Manchester City down. They did really well in that.

It has been revealed that “It was a deserved draw, ultimately we leave here with a bitter taste in our mouths, but I told the lads that the belief, the courage is necessary in Europe, as there are spaces to play in. After this, we must prepare in the best way for Sassuolo, tonight was a good training session above all for our defence.”.

Considering the circumstances, it is remarkable to see Napoli leaving Manchester City feeling regret, as they were decimated with barely any options to come off the bench.

“We should be happy with the point, which is the most important thing, but also the performance. There were moments when we should’ve made more of their high line, and had a couple of good situations, but we were against a very strong opponent. The lads applied themselves brilliantly.”.

Allegri was asked if this was his most satisfying evening yet on the Napoli bench, especially as there haven’t been many high points yet in his tenure since taking over from Antonio Conte.

In a recent development, “I am above all happy for the lads. When you play in the Champions League, you need that extra belief, to even be arrogant, and trust your abilities.”.

This was an emotional return to Manchester for Kevin De Bruyne, who was given a hero’s welcome by his former fans, and a standing ovation when substituted late on.

According to recent reports, “Unfortunately, age waits for no man, but he is an extraordinary player. It made me sad to take him off today, as he rarely makes a mistake with the ball at his feet. Players like De Bruyne and Luka Modric, for those who love football and admire the sport, they represent something special.”.

De Bruyne will be out of contract in June 2027, but there are multiple reports he could leave for PSV Eindhoven in January.

“We’ll discuss it with the club, but he is a very professional lad, and I think he will remain until June,” assured Allegri.

Napoli have been leaking goals all season, and Allegri took responsibility for their struggles.

“I think in the first part of the season, above all for my responsibility, we didn’t do enough to prepare defensively. We conceded too many really silly goals, for example against Bodo/Glimt when conceding for 4-3 straight after going 4-2 up.

Industry observers note that “That is a bad sign, it is a sign of a lack of respect and humility from the team in certain moments of the match. We made Manchester City sweat to score goals today, they had to do something extraordinary, and that is how it should be, with this determination in the tackle and total concentration in every game,” concluded the coach.

It has been revealed that there has long been a debate about the true quality of Major League Soccer. Thomas Muller recently caused a stir when he spoke about his issues with the United States' premier football competition.

Sources indicate that the former Bayern Munich star, at the moment with Vancouver Whitecaps, has spent just over 12 months playing for the Canadian club and has outlined his main issue with MLS. He claimed there isn't enough pressure for players due to a lack of jeopardy when it comes to relegation:.

Recent findings suggest that "There is no big pressure. There is... 'oh yeah we do a rebuild'. Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you're fighting relegation.

Industry observers note that "You lose budget for the next year, you lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans. The pressure... the players maybe have no contracts for next year when you go down.

Sources indicate that "So the playing style changes when you play a bottom of the league team in Europe. They fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling... because of the system, the playing style is a bit more optimistic or careless defensively. That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up.".

The comments quickly went viral, sparking much debate about where MLS ranks among the best leagues in world football. With that in mind, it's interesting to learn what Steven Gerrard thought of MLS during his stint at LA Galaxy.

Gerrard is one of the greatest English footballers of all time. He spent almost his entire career at Liverpool – famously winning the 2005 Champions League – before moving to MLS for his final few years. Between 2015 and 2016, the midfielder played 39 games for LA Galaxy before retiring at the age of 36.

Speaking after the end of his first MLS season in the United States, Gerrard concluded that the competition was "a lot better than I initially thought." He claimed it was no 'retirement league', explaining:.

"If people think they can come here just to have a holiday and retire, they are going to have a mistake because they won't perform well and they won't do their team justice because I have had to come here and work hard and get fit, make sure that I keep performing to play well.".

In a recent development, "A lot of people talk about the MLS, about the level, but for me a lot of them are wrong. Until you come here and sample it yourself, you see how strong it is and how fit and professional the players are.

"Every single game is a different challenge, certainly on the road you come up against places and teams where it is very hot and very humid; some teams play on astroturf. So each game is very tricky and very difficult. The games at home, we've had a very strong team and we've enjoyed some really strong performances.".

Industry observers note that gerrard concluded: "You know a lot of TV channels all around the world have started to follow the MLS. A lot of big players from Europe have come over to try and strengthen the league. I am sure with time it will be continuing to grow and become a lot stronger.".

While Muller may well have a point about the league needing more jeopardy, it's interesting to learn that a player of Gerrard's quality held MLS in such high regard.

He wasn't the first iconic Englishman to play for LA Galaxy, with David Beckham paving the way on that front. However, Gerrard lasted only 39 games, compared to Beckham's 124. Truthfully, the Liverpool legend struggled to bring his best form to the US, which perhaps explains why he retired not that long after arriving.

The new Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

  • When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.
  • The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Recent findings suggest that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some big money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the big day,’ claims a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective new head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

According to recent reports, there was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is mentioned to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

It has been revealed that media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

It has been revealed that there was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is noted to have gone according to initiative as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his newly introduced job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

The US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Sources indicate that pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Sources indicate that responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino worked with his latest players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At a time when press freedom is under pressure and international newsrooms are shrinking, the Werner Holzer Prize celebrates a profession that many consider indispensable to democracy: foreign correspondence.

Presented in honor of Werner Holzer, the veteran reporter and former editor-in-chief of the German daily newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau, this year's award coincided with what would have been his 100th birthday. Holzer spent decades reporting from some of the world's most vital hot spots and championing international journalism.

At the award ceremony in Frankfurt's Römer, the city's historic town hall, Mayor Mike Josef recalled that fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and freedom of the press were first enshrined for all Germans by the Frankfurt Parliament in the nearby Paulskirche in 1848.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the 2026 winners reflect the breadth and ambition of the award. First prize went to Katja Gloger, a veteran Russia correspondent who moved to Moscow in 1989 and accompanied Vladimir Putin during the early years of his presidency.

In her recent nonfiction book, "The Failure: An Investigative Report of Germany's Russia Policy," Gloger and co-author Georg Mascolo offer a searing critique of the misjudgments and illusions that shaped German policy toward Russia for decades.

Second prize was awarded to DW journalist and presenter Jaafar Abdul Karim. His talk show JaafarTalk reaches millions of viewers across the Arab world and in Germany. Whether in Tunis, Beirut or Cairo, Abdul Karim tackles subjects that are often considered taboo.

It has been revealed that A research grant went to freelance journalist Luise Land, whose current project explores why her German-Namibian family still owns extensive landholdings in Namibia today. By tracing that history, she examines the enduring legacy of the genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples by German colonial forces in the early 20th century.

It has been revealed that "Katja Gloger is one of the leading foreign policy reporters. For decades, she has been among the foremost experts on Russia and speaks out on uncomfortable truths," the jury stated on Friday, explaining its decision to honor Gloger. "Like almost no one else, she has gained access to the very heart of the Kremlin's power elite — from Mikhail Gorbachev to Vladimir Putin.".

At the prize-giving ceremony, Gloger delivered a passionate plea for more journalism — and more international coverage — in the German press. "We must defend trustworthy, reliable and fact-based journalism with everything in our power," she mentioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, gloger worked for Reporters Without Borders for 12 years. "The latest rankings show that only one in 100 people can get their information from free, independent journalism and a free, independent press. That demonstrates what's at stake," she noted.

The prize winner also mentioned she would dedicate the award to journalists in exile and to her colleagues at Novaya Gazeta, the independent Russian newspaper long known for its critical reporting on the Kremlin. Earlier this week, the paper was forced to shut down its operations in Russia and leave its Moscow newsroom.

Industry observers note that in his acceptance speech, Jaafar Abdul Karim stated journalism has become more challenging and exhausting than ever. The DW host spoke of hatred and incitement, attacks and threats, both online and offline, in the regions he reports on as well as in Germany.

Such pressure, he said, takes a personal toll — yet giving up is not an option. "When I listen to my heart, I know I have to keep going," he said. The answer, he argued, is a form of journalism that fosters dialogue, embraces multiple perspectives and helps bridge divides rather than deepen them.

"I firmly believe in the power of dialogue, today more than ever. That's why we must talk to one another. Even when it gets difficult. Even when we disagree. Or perhaps precisely because of that," he noted.

Listening doesn't mean agreeing, and understanding doesn't mean being in agreement. "Especially now, in times of polarization, when those who believe they're always right are often the loudest, we as journalists have a special responsibility. When everyone is just shouting into their own bubbles or communities, we need journalists who connect these bubbles with one another," he stated.

The jury praised Abdul Karim for creating programs at DW that reach millions of young people across the Arab world and in Germany. "His journalism fosters dialogue between countries, between generations, and between religions. He has set latest standards," the jury stated.

Industry observers note that so far in 2026, JaafarTalk has already garnered more than 1.1 billion views across all platforms, and its community has grown to more than 9 million followers. Its motto: "Diversity fosters dialogue.".

Recent findings suggest that "We need fact-based journalism that promotes dialogue and reflects the diversity of our society," Abdul Karim stressed. "By that, I mean an honest and open dialogue in which we do not look away or remain silent. On the contrary, we must take a clear stand against racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, discrimination, sexism, and hate speech — no matter which side they come from.".

Paul Scholes has revealed that Ruud van Nistelrooy was the best striker he shared the pitch with during his career. Scholes spent all 19 seasons of his senior career under Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United, where he made 714 appearances, scored 153 goals and provided another 83 assists. Those achievements have helped cement his reputation as one of the greatest players to have ever put on the red jersey of Man United.

During his time at Old Trafford, Scholes helped the Red Devils win 26 trophies, including 11 Premier League titles and two Champions League crowns, a haul that ranks him among the most decorated players in football history. He became renowned for his exceptional vision and range of passing, regularly delivering the ball with remarkable accuracy, timing and precision, traits that place him among the greatest midfielders of the Premier League era.

It has been revealed that scholes had the opportunity to play with some of the greatest strikers Man United have ever had throughout his career, from Andy Cole and Dwight Yorke to Eric Cantona and the club's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney. Even so, none developed the same on-field understanding with him as Dutch striker van Nistelrooy.

Although he played alongside a number of Manchester United icons, Scholes explained to BBC Sounds during an episode of 606 Savage Social that one player stood out as the teammate he had a much stronger on-pitch connection with above all others.

In a recent development, speaking about van Nistelrooy, Scholes described a natural understanding between the pair. He knew where the striker would make his runs and precisely when to play the pass to give his Dutch teammate the clearest chance of scoring.

Sources indicate that "That's an easy one. I don't want to disrespect any of the other forwards - because I've played with some amazing players, especially at United. Andy Cole, Dwight Yorke, Ole Gunnar [Solskjaer] at the time, but I always thought I had the best connection with Ruud van Nistelrooy. I played the season with him, and I think I scored 20 goals playing as a ten. I knew what he wanted, I knew the runs he'd make and where he wanted the ball. What a finisher. That man was just hungry. His life depended on scoring goals. He was the one I felt I had a great connection with.".

In a recent development, scholes and van Nistelrooy played together 165 times and combined for 16 goal contributions, during the Dutchman's five seasons at Old Trafford. Nevertheless, he made a significant mark on both the club and English football, scoring 95 goals and adding 14 assists across 150 Premier League appearances. He also claimed the Golden Boot and Player of the Season awards in 2002/03.

His record is one reason he is so often regarded as one of the greatest strikers in Premier League history. Few forwards seemed so completely devoted to finding the net, making his relatively short spell in English football a disappointment for fans who wanted to see more.

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

Industry observers note that this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

It has been revealed that this was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

Recent findings suggest that “I have to take the responsibility,” he said. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the blueprint. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

It has been revealed that “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the initiative disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

Newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

Recent findings suggest that if they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight upcoming signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat quickly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

There was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Sources indicate that for Newcastle, a win tonight would take them up to seventh, just two points behind Chelsea in fourth. Despite the heavy away defeats and unconvincing performances, that would be an impressive start for a latest manager. Matthias Jaissle has already felt the full force of the contrasting emotions on Tyneside in his three months in charge but big questions hang over his team. Newcastle and Everton meet for the second time in matter of days as the Premier League weekend concludes in the north east at St James’ Park. These teams encountered each other on Thursday night in the League Cup, where Everton won 3-1 at the Hill Dickinson to progress to the quarter-finals in that competition.

Newcastle, who won 2-0 at Crystal Palace in their last league outing, come into this game in 12th, with the chance to rise to seventh with a victory tonight. Their boss Matthias Jaissle has called on his players to use the defeat against Everton on Thursday as fuel for tonight.

“Now it is about taking that frustration into motivation for Monday and having that approach for the rematch,” Jaissle mentioned. “We take it as a long-term journey, and our approach is to make progress, to see improvements. Now it is time to learn fast out of the mistakes that we just did. [There are] other phases where we can already see that we improved and this is something we can count on, we can build on, the good part. But football is also in the end about results so you need to avoid these simple mistakes.”.

Industry observers note that everton, who have not won in the league since a 1-0 victory over Ipswich back in September, begin the night in 14th but, like Newcastle, could rise to seventh with a win. There are just two points that separate Bournemouth in seventh and Everton in 14th. Despite getting the better of Newcastle the other night, Everton manager David Moyes has warned that game will count for nothing tonight.

It has been revealed that “It is a different ball game,” Moyes said. “Go to St James’ Park, on a Monday evening, they will get a crowd up there, you always know you are up against it. But we will go with confidence. We have played Newcastle a couple of times this year and done well, so we have to try and continue it. But Newcastle have got some really, really good players and players you have to concern yourself about.”.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton’s squad for that League Cup victory because of an unauthorised absence from training and the 31-year-old is not expected to be involved tonight.

In a recent development, these sides were involved in a dramatic fixture on this ground last season. Everton claimed a 3-2 victory, with Thierno Barry earning them all three points in the 83rd minute, moments after Jacob Murphy had equalised for Newcastle. The final 2026/27 Championship table has been predicted in full by a Supercomputer following the opening months of the latest season.

West Ham United, Burnley and Wolverhampton Wanderers dropped into English football's second tier after suffering relegation from the Premier League last season. That trio - which, for the first time in four years, was not made up of the same three clubs that had won promotion the season before - will all be desperate to bounce straight back at the first attempt.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Lincoln City, Cardiff City and Bolton Wanderers would surely be more than content with consolidation after securing their Championship status on the back of impressive League One campaigns. For those clubs, simply keeping their heads above water and establishing themselves at a higher level may be viewed as success.

However, if the Supercomputer's projections, courtesy of Opta (as of 24/11/26), are to be believed, there could be plenty of twists and turns ahead. The Championship rarely follows a script and has a habit of throwing up surprises when least expected, and this predicted final table suggests several clubs may be in for a rollercoaster ride. In fact, the standings look markedly different from how many supporters and pundits would have expected the season to unfold.

It has been revealed that preston North End have been perennial mid-table finishers in the Championship for over a decade. However, after a dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign, Opta's Supercomputer thinks they will finish rock bottom this campaign and drop to League One alongside Derby County and Watford.

According to recent reports, lincoln City are riding the crest of promotion, but it is set to be a tough campaign for them, having lost manager Michael Skubala to Bristol City in the off-season. Wins against Bolton, Bristol City, Preston and Burnley helped put them up into a much safer predicted position initially, but a 4-0 thrashing at the hands of Charlton has them hovering just above the bottom three.

Industry observers note that burnley, who were relegated from the Premier League in 25/26, are expected to finish 20th with just 49 points. That would be a huge disappointment for the Lancashire side, who would have had aspirations of returning to England's top tier at the first time of asking.

Charlton Athletic enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2026/27 campaign, picking up victories against Derby County, West Ham United and Preston. They couldn't maintain that incredible run, though, plummeting down the table following an 11-match winless run. After beating Sheffield United and Lincoln, they now sit slightly higher up the table.

Bolton Wanderers are back in the Championship following a long time away. After winning five of their opening 16 games, they're expected to avoid relegation.

After coming from 4-1 down to beat Burnley 5-4, Cardiff City have lost their following two games. They are not expected to finish 16th, one place above Bristol City.

It has been revealed that the Robins have firmly established themselves in the English second tier, qualifying for the playoffs in the 2024/25 season. However, despite success in recent years, the Supercomputer thinks they will struggle and finish in the bottom half.

Blackburn Rovers have flirted with relegation in recent years, with fans of the club regularly venting their frustration with their owners, the Venky's. They always find a way to escape the drop, though, and are expected to have more than enough to stay up once again this season.

Millwall came so close to achieving promotion to England's top tier in 2025/26, eventually having to settle for third place and a spot in the playoffs. Opta's Supercomputer thinks they will just miss out on a playoff berth this time round.

Wrexham narrowly failed to make the playoffs last season as they finished seventh. After a very slow start to the season, they are again expected to miss out, with the Supercomputer predicting them to finish in a disappointing 13th with 64 points.

According to recent reports, portsmouth were at threat of relegation in the 2025/26 campaign, but they avoided the drop after improving in the final months. They've had an impressive start to the campaign and are being predicted to finish in the top half, having just beaten West Ham.

In a recent development, sheffield United endured a torrid campaign in 25/26. At one point, it looked as if they would have a battle on their hands to maintain their Championship status. They eventually finished mid-table, and they are predicted to end this campaign in a similar position.

The 2026/27 season will be the first year in which six teams qualify for the playoffs, expanded from four.

Norwich City ended the 2025/26 campaign on fire and would have been expecting to start 26/27 in the same manner. After an awful start to the campaign, they've recovered and now occupy 11th place in the real table. The Supercomputer thinks they'll end up finishing one spot higher, but still just outside the playoff places.

Recent findings suggest that swansea City had an electric start to the season and led the way after 10 matches. However, after just one win in their seven matches, they are now predicted to finish ninth with 70 points.

Sources indicate that queens Park Rangers have had a decent start to the campaign, picking up 28 points from their opening 17 matches. The Supercomputer thinks they'll fall short in their bid to make the playoffs, though.

Recent findings suggest that stoke City spent major in the 2026 summer transfer window, with Ethan Galbraith and George Hirst among the players who arrived for big money. Their decision to spend big has paid dividends so far, with the club currently flying high in third. The Supercomputer thinks they'll just about scrape into the playoffs, though.

In a recent development, west Ham, the favourites in the eyes of many to win the Championship and return to the Premier League at the first time of asking before a ball was kicked, had an awful start to the campaign. They failed to win their opening three matches, with draws against Burnley and Watford, as well as a 2-1 defeat to Charlton at the London Stadium.

The Hammers climbed up the table after that poor start, but after their form took another turn for the worse once more, Nuno Espirito Santo lost his job in early November and was replaced by Scott Parker. After going winless in Parker's first four matches in charge, they are now expected to miss out on an automatic promotion berth.

Recent findings suggest that tom Brady is no longer at Birmingham City, but the Blues are still expected to have a shot at promotion this season. They are being tipped to finish the campaign in fourth with 76 points, one place above Midlands rivals West Bromwich Albion.

According to recent reports, southampton started the campaign on -4 points after they were punished for spying on several other teams in the 2025/26 campaign. Despite that disadvantage, the Supercomputer thinks the Saints will finish third after winning nine of their opening 17 matches.

Recent findings suggest that wolverhampton Wanderers boast an enviable mix of youthful excitement and older, wiser players, so with the resources at their disposal, it would be a shock if they didn't get that automatic promotion place. The Supercomputer thinks they will just about seal their return to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

Middlesbrough, who were beaten by Hull City in the playoff final in May, will be delighted if they don't have to go through the playoffs again this term as they chase a return to the Premier League. Despite dropping points to Watford in their last outing, Kim Hellberg's side are predicted to be crowned champions with 82 points.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season.
  • The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that the move had been signalled earlier in the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season. The deal gives the Spanish club its first affiliate in South America before the Ecuadorian team steps up to Serie A in 2027.

The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.

It has been revealed that the move had been signalled earlier in the year. On Friday 20 February 2026, Atlético said it would share sporting, institutional and commercial expertise with Atlético FC and might take a stake in the following months, El Comercio reported.

Regarded as Ecuador’s largest non-profit organisation, the Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil operates in all 24 of the country’s provinces.

The club’s route into Serie B was unusual. It took over the place of Atlético Vinotinto, which could not use it because its affiliate Vinotinto FC had been relegated. The team also changed its name from Atlético JBG to Atlético FC.

Promotion came on 15 October 2026 with a 1-0 win over Independiente Juniors. Fidel Martínez scored the goal. A week later, on Thursday 22 October, a 2-2 draw against Cuenca Juniors at the Estadio Alejandro Serrano sealed the title. That match was the ninth round of the promotion hexagonal.

Recent findings suggest that across the campaign the side scored 39 goals and conceded 21. It became the 37th different club to win Ecuador’s Serie B. The team is coached by Carlos Santamarina, who comes from Atlético’s academy.

The promotion also reshapes the city’s football map. Guayaquil will have four clubs in the 2027 Serie A: Atlético FC, Barcelona SC, Emelec and Guayaquil City.

Mexico and Canada already host clubs in the Madrid side’s network of linked teams, through Atlético de San Luis and Atlético Ottawa.

The investment builds on years of groundwork in Ecuador. Atlético and the Junta signed their original strategic agreement on Monday 24 July 2023 at the charity’s sports complex. Under that deal, the club’s academy would apply its coaching model to the Junta’s football division. At the time, that division served 2,500 children from vulnerable backgrounds.

In a recent development, in June 2026 the club put the number of young players at more than 14,000. That same month, chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín visited the academy’s Guayaquil base. With the Junta’s delegation, he watched an Atlético FC match and greeted Santamarina.

El Atlético Fútbol Club se une a la familia rojiblanca.

Nuestro club hace efectiva la adquisición del 50% del equipo ecuatoriano, que logró el ascenso a la Serie A en octubre de la mano del técnico de la Academia Carlos Santamarina.

It has been revealed that ¡Bienvenidos, @AtleticoFCec! ❤️🤍.

— Atlético de Madrid (@Atleti) November 13, 2026.

For Atlético, the stake creates a direct link between that youth work and a senior professional team.

It has been revealed that the board holds its first meeting next week. It will elect a president proposed by Atlético and appoint a general manager.

Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1267 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it was 5:55 a.m.
  • In a recent development, following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

In a recent development, following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

According to recent reports, but here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

If the upcoming debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

Industry observers note that this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

To understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

Sources indicate that what's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Recent findings suggest that the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

According to recent reports, the Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

Anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on latest debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

It has been revealed that the key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

It has been revealed that at the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

This would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

The prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cesc Fabregas feels Como really made a Champions League statement in their 1-0 victory over AEK Athens, and jokes that they can ‘sell Luis Milla for €20m in January’ after his goal.

The Lariani struggled to break down AEK Athens at the Stadio Sinigaglia this evening, especially after Lucas Da Cunha drilled a penalty off target in the first half.

Also hitting the woodwork a couple of times, they eventually found the winner thanks to a Luis Milla curler into the far top corner from outside the box.

“It is a victory that was crucial for us, because the level of the Champions League is very high and demanding,” Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia.

It has been revealed that “Whether we won or not today, we proved that this team does not struggle to raise the bar when the match takes on a different context. In our five games, we were always competitive, and the most important thing I wanted to see this season was that.

It has been revealed that “The results are going our way and we need to keep going. Serie A remains the most notable thing for us, but I cannot deny that it is truly wonderful to experience Champions League nights at the Sinigaglia.”.

Milla got the only goal of the game, and his path to Como was not an easy one, as it took several attempts to finally sign the midfielder.

“We signed him for €6m, maybe we’ll sell him in January for €20m,” smiled Fabregas with Milla waiting nearby for his interview.

“No, I’m kidding, he’s a great player, has had a high level for a long time, his career saw him constantly improve and now he has the kind of character and experience, he is above all a strong presence in the locker room.”.

The Lariani ran a few risks late on too against AEK Athens, so Fabio Capello in the Sky Sport Italia studio asked if Fabregas was worried by their fitness levels in the final 20 minutes?

Recent findings suggest that “I am always worried! I don’t have your experience to be calm in these situations! The Champions League is of such a level that you can pay for any tiny mistake,” replied the coach.

“The truth is, there aren’t many of us, because there were eight players missing today due to injury and the UEFA squad list limitations, so I think for the first time in my career I only made three substitutions today.

“I did like the character of the squad, the mentality and hunger. Obviously, there are always things to improve, but I liked the approach.”.

This success means Como have won four of their five Champions League games so far this season, losing only 3-2 away to Feyenoord, and have practically guaranteed at least a spot in the play-offs.
